issues.description: The problem statement's UML lists only two attributes for ExcellenceLand (excellencyLevel: double, excellentEnough: boolean), but task text separately specifies an additional private attribute rides of type List<Ride>. The general constructor-order rule in the statement requires constructor parameters to follow the UML attribute order, yet the solution implements ExcellenceLand with a constructor whose parameter order is (List<Ride> rides, boolean excellentEnough, double excellencyLevel). This conflicts with the stated rule (which would imply double, boolean, ...) and leaves students unclear where the 'rides' parameter belongs and which parameter order to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and make consistent: either (A) update the UML in problem_statement.md to include the 'rides' attribute in the intended position (so constructor ordering is unambiguous), or (B) explicitly state in the task that the constructor should have parameters in the order (List<Ride> rides, boolean excellentEnough, double excellencyLevel) to match the solution/tests. Then align the template and solution constructor signatures with that clarified ordering.
